note: Trigger eval set. should_trigger=true cases must invoke llm-council (multi-model deliberation). The should_trigger=false case is a near-miss routine edit that must NOT pay 4x tokens for a council. A Workflow sub-agent cannot nest a Workflow, so a live 4-model council run is NOT executed here — the oracle runs the heavyweight live council separately as the runtime proof.

evals.prompt: convene the council on whether we should pick a serverless (Convex functions) vs a long-running Node service architecture for the new realtime sync layer — this is hard to undo once we commit the schema
evals.expected_output: Workflow council runs: four Claude models answer the architecture question independently, peer-review anonymously, Opus president returns a Verdict + Why + Where the council disagreed + Confidence.

evals.prompt: @council: our verify worker says the auth fix is PASS but the secaudit flagged it FAIL. is this verify verdict trustworthy or not?
evals.expected_output: Council convened as a tie-break across contradictory adversarial verdicts; president verdict preserves the dissent (the FAIL position) as a tracked risk rather than dropping it.

evals.prompt: I want a second opinion from multiple models on this database-sharding design before I commit it — it's a one-way door
evals.expected_output: llm-council triggers on the explicit multi-model second-opinion + irreversible (one-way door) signal; four models deliberate, Opus president synthesizes with dissent.

evals.prompt: rename the variable `usr` to `user` in src/auth/login.ts and save the file
evals.expected_output: No council. This is a routine one-line edit — a single agent does it directly. Convening four models + a peer-review round + a president would be 4x the cost for zero benefit.
